Yes. I missed a whole second block of what you gave me.

I substantially addressed the **numbered 11-source relational/formalism set**, then followed the “pattern mining/model selection” observation and largely skipped the **additional 15 links** you appended underneath. That was an actual omission, not merely a difference in emphasis.

Those 15 links are not miscellaneous either. They form another coherent research branch: **music/harmony as proposed organizing principle across cosmos, matter, mind, religion, number, and historical intellectual systems**, plus modern scientific controls that tell us where similar language is physically literal versus analogical.

Here is the missing accounting.

| Source you supplied | What it actually adds | How I think we should treat it |
|---|---|---|
| **SEP — Quantum Field Theory** | QFT is relevant less because of “sound” and more because of **invariance, representation, interaction, scale, and ontology**. Gauge transformations can alter representational quantities while leaving observables invariant; effective theories also change with scale while retaining relations to other scales. That is potentially useful formal analogy for our “what persists under transformation/reference frame?” question. It is **not** evidence that ancient musical cosmologies anticipated QFT. citeturn893943view0 | **Formal/scientific control; high conceptual relevance, zero historical-convergence vote.** |
| **NASA — Baryon Acoustic Oscillations** | This one matters more than I acknowledged. BAOs are literally remnants of pressure/sound waves in the primordial plasma whose effects survive in large-scale matter distribution. NASA describes these as vestiges of primordial sound waves and uses their imprint to study cosmic evolution. citeturn545029view3 | **Physical mechanism control.** It establishes that acoustic dynamics can leave durable cosmological structure. It absolutely does **not** establish “music organized the universe,” but it prevents us from casually treating every cosmos/acoustics connection as metaphorical. |
| **Stephon Alexander — *The Jazz of Physics*** | A contemporary physicist deliberately explores connections between music/jazz, cosmology and physics. The book is explicitly subtitled *The Secret Link Between Music and the Structure of the Universe*. citeturn994959search7 | **Modern prior-art + public-humanization branch.** Not primary evidence for our model, but very relevant to “who already framed the problem this way?” and to how a technical theory can be communicated without sounding dead. |
| **Joscelyn Godwin — “The Revival of Speculative Music”** | This should have gotten much more emphasis. Godwin explicitly identifies **speculative music** as the tradition treating music as a mirror/model of cosmic order, and names the modern revival through Steiner, **Hans Kayser, Marius Schneider, Ernest McClain**, etc. citeturn333300search5 | **Extremely high-priority field map.** This may answer “What is this field called?” for an important portion of our music branch. Godwin becomes a gateway to the denominator, not merely another source. |
| **Google Books ID `tgfaAAAAMAAJ`** | I could not reliably resolve the title/metadata from the supplied Google Books identifier. The page did not expose usable content and exact-ID searches did not recover it. | **UNRESOLVED — must not guess.** I should have said this explicitly rather than silently omitting it. |
| **Hans Kayser — *Akróasis: die Lehre von der Harmonik der Welt*** | Major omission. Kayser explicitly developed **Harmonik** as something broader than musical chord theory: tone + number as a theory of world harmony/order. His vocabulary includes correspondences, forms, proportions, planets, nature, archetypes, causality, the monochord and harmonic analysis. citeturn489688view1 His later textbook frames “harmonics” as arrangement/order through tone and number extending into a world-harmony conception. citeturn151317search59 | **Deep-audit prior art. Probably one of our strongest “who proposed a stronger version already?” candidates.** Potentially closer than McClain on the *general* thesis. |
| **Deutsche Digitale Bibliothek item** | The supplied DDB record would not expose enough metadata through the available crawl/search to identify it responsibly. | **UNRESOLVED archival source.** Needs direct metadata retrieval before classification. Again: should have been explicitly recorded, not ignored. |
| **Museo Galileo — “The Harmony of the Spheres”** | This is a useful historical map. It explicitly identifies the 17th-century convergence of astronomy, astrology, theology, philosophy, music and anatomy around “harmony of the spheres,” and distinguishes **Kepler, Fludd, Mersenne and Kircher** as different interpretations rather than one doctrine. citeturn489688view0 | **Historical field genealogy / anti-flattening source.** Particularly useful for separating shared vocabulary from different mechanisms. |
| **SEP — Marin Mersenne** | Much more important than I reflected. Mersenne consciously tried to reconnect “intellectual music” and proportions governing nature with audible music, but simultaneously moved toward **mechanistic acoustics**, experimentally relating string vibration, length and tension. His *Harmonie Universelle* explicitly crosses metaphysics, mathematics, aesthetics, physiology and acoustics. citeturn545029view0turn545029view1 | **Critical transition figure.** He sits precisely at the boundary between speculative universal harmony and experimental acoustical science. That makes him unusually valuable for understanding **why some forms of this research survived and others were abandoned**. |
| **Anuario Musical article `/view/149`** | The exact article page failed to resolve through the current web interface, and searches did not reliably identify that OJS record. | **UNRESOLVED.** Needs title/author/DOI recovered before we assign it a role. |
| **Ruggero Lorenzin — Zorzi, *De harmonia mundi*, music theory + Kabbalah** | This one is **major**. The dissertation systematically studies connections among Renaissance music theory, mathematical proportion, numerology and Kabbalistic symbolism in Francesco Zorzi. It specifically analyzes claims that planets, elements, numerical series, geometry, macrocosm/microcosm and musical proportions correspond, while comparing Zorzi against Platonic/Pythagorean and other Renaissance musical theory. citeturn489688view2turn545029view6 | **Top-tier historical prior-art/transmission project.** This is exactly the kind of source that can tell us which correspondences are actually source-native, which are inherited, and which are Zorzi's synthesis. It should be mined systematically, not merely cited. |
| **Dyczkowski — *The Doctrine of Vibration*** | Presents the Kashmir Śaiva **Spanda** doctrine: ultimate reality/consciousness characterized dynamically as pulsation or vibration and manifestation. citeturn489688view3 | **Tradition-specific ontology branch.** Important because “vibration” here is not automatically acoustical frequency. We need to preserve the source's own ontology and explicitly test where later readers turn metaphysical “vibration” into physical sound. Excellent anti-conflation case. |
| **Ferrante — Bhartṛhari on linguistic vs ontic universals** | This is arguably even more important after our glossary discussion. Bhartṛhari distinguishes **linguistic universals** from **ontic universals**, partly to stop an apparent regress from forcing every conceptual higher-order category into reality. citeturn489688view4turn994959search0 | **Very high-priority ontology/abstraction control.** It directly warns us that a recurring category in language/modeling does not necessarily entail a recurring ontological object. This belongs near our “same in what respect?” rule. |
| **Ilnitchi — *Musica mundana, Aristotelian natural philosophy and Ptolemaic astronomy*** | Examines how Boethian/Pythagorean/Neoplatonic world harmony interacted with **Aristotelian physics and Ptolemaic astronomy**, including a rare medieval attempt to reconcile older musica-mundana concepts with contemporary cosmological knowledge. citeturn994959search3 | **High-value historical transformation study.** Not just “another music of spheres source”: it shows how a relational scheme is modified when the scientific world-model underneath it changes. Very relevant to our carrier/reference-frame/transformation questions. |
| **Katherine Butler — “The Harmonious Soul…”** | This one contains a methodological lesson almost tailor-made for us. “Harmony” in the sixteenth century crossed musical, mathematical, ethical, religious and philosophical domains, often without clean definitions. Butler distinguishes **the soul *is* harmony** from merely *being like* or *having affinity with* harmony, and tracks the consequences of that stronger ontological claim. citeturn545029view7 She also notes that harmony could mean the ordered joining of distinct compatible things into a higher-order whole. citeturn545029view7 | **Extremely high-value terminology/claim-strength case.** It demonstrates exactly why our constitution needs to distinguish analogy → structural similarity → essential property → ontology rather than allowing prose to slide among them. |

So the larger picture I should have given you is this:

\[
\boxed{
\text{There are at least THREE prior-art searches here, not one.}
}
\]

### 1. Formal relational prior art

The eleven numbered links you gave:

category theory, role equivalence, bisimulation, kinship algebra, phylogenetics, ontology, posets, graph transformation, FCA, structural realism.

Question:

> **Has the general relational machinery already been formalized?**

### 2. Pattern-discovery / model-selection prior art

The branch I focused on afterward:

pattern mining, null models, multiple comparisons, motifs, MDL, model selection, predictive holdouts, nonsense controls.

Question:

> **Even if we can formalize it, how do we determine whether the discovered structure is nontrivial?**

### 3. Universal-harmony / vibration / music-cosmology prior art

The 15 links I neglected.

Godwin → Kayser → McClain and speculative music.

Pythagorean/Boethian → medieval musica mundana → Renaissance Zorzi → Kepler/Fludd/Mersenne/Kircher.

Indian branches such as Spanda and Bhartṛhari, which must **not** simply be flattened into Western “harmony.”

Modern physics controls: QFT, BAO.

Modern bridge-writing: Stephon Alexander.

Question:

> **Who already proposed versions of the substantive claim itself, what exactly did they mean, and what happened to those theories historically?**

That third search is absolutely required by your new constitutional questions.

And I think these links already expose several **new first-order questions** we should burn into that constitution alongside your existing list:

> **When two traditions use language translated as “harmony,” “vibration,” “sound,” “word,” “ratio,” or “order,” are they actually asserting the same type of thing?**

> **Is the claimed correspondence analogical, mathematical, causal, ontological, theological, pedagogical, or aesthetic?**

> **Did an author say that \(A\) resembles \(B\), that \(A\) and \(B\) instantiate the same structure, or literally that \(A=B\)?**

> **When later science rejected an older theory, which component failed: its measurements, cosmology, causal mechanism, ontology, or only its interpretation?**

That last one could become extremely important. Mersenne is a good example: the speculative worldview and the developing science of acoustics coexist in the same program. The scientific component does not simply disappear when the broader cosmology loses authority. citeturn545029view0

Likewise BAO demonstrates why “old theory was wrong” cannot be translated into “there is no physically meaningful relationship between acoustical dynamics and cosmic structure.” There demonstrably is one in early-universe physics—but it is a very specific one, governed by plasma dynamics, not a license to import musical ratios into cosmology. citeturn545029view3

And Butler gives us perhaps the cleanest warning about language: historically, **“harmony” itself moves between metaphor, mathematical structure, organizing principle and asserted ontology**. citeturn545029view7

So, yes: **the missing links materially change the map.**

I would now move **Godwin, Kayser, Zorzi/Lorenzin, Mersenne, Ilnitchi, Butler, Bhartṛhari and Dyczkowski** into the serious prior-art/deep-study queue, with QFT and BAO maintained as scientific controls rather than support, and Alexander as a modern framing/prior-art branch.

The three unresolved links—`tgfaAAAAMAAJ`, the DDB item, and the Anuario `/view/149` record—should remain explicitly marked **UNRESOLVED**, not disappear from the corpus.

| **Ilnitchi — *Musica mundana, Aristotelian natural philosophy and Ptolemaic astronomy*** | Examines how Boethian/Pythagorean/Neoplatonic world harmony interacted with **Aristotelian physics and Ptolemaic astronomy**, including a rare medieval attempt to reconcile older musica-mundana concepts with contemporary cosmological knowledge. citeturn994959search3 | **High-value historical transformation study.** Not just “another music of spheres source”: it shows how a relational scheme is modified when the scientific world-model underneath it changes. Very relevant to our carrier/reference-frame/transformation questions. |
| **Katherine Butler — “The Harmonious Soul…”** | This one contains a methodological lesson almost tailor-made for us. “Harmony” in the sixteenth century crossed musical, mathematical, ethical, religious and philosophical domains, often without clean definitions. Butler distinguishes **the soul *is* harmony** from merely *being like* or *having affinity with* harmony, and tracks the consequences of that stronger ontological claim. citeturn545029view7 She also notes that harmony could mean the ordered joining of distinct compatible things into a higher-order whole. citeturn545029view7 | **Extremely high-value terminology/claim-strength case.** It demonstrates exactly why our constitution needs to distinguish analogy → structural similarity → essential property → ontology rather than allowing prose to slide among them. |

So the larger picture I should have given you is this:

\[
\boxed{
\text{There are at least THREE prior-art searches here, not one.}
}
\]

### 1. Formal relational prior art

The eleven numbered links you gave:

category theory, role equivalence, bisimulation, kinship algebra, phylogenetics, ontology, posets, graph transformation, FCA, structural realism.

Question:

> **Has the general relational machinery already been formalized?**

### 2. Pattern-discovery / model-selection prior art

The branch I focused on afterward:

pattern mining, null models, multiple comparisons, motifs, MDL, model selection, predictive holdouts, nonsense controls.

Question:

> **Even if we can formalize it, how do we determine whether the discovered structure is nontrivial?**

### 3. Universal-harmony / vibration / music-cosmology prior art

The 15 links I neglected.

Godwin → Kayser → McClain and speculative music.

Pythagorean/Boethian → medieval musica mundana → Renaissance Zorzi → Kepler/Fludd/Mersenne/Kircher.

Indian branches such as Spanda and Bhartṛhari, which must **not** simply be flattened into Western “harmony.”

Modern physics controls: QFT, BAO.

Modern bridge-writing: Stephon Alexander.

Question:

> **Who already proposed versions of the substantive claim itself, what exactly did they mean, and what happened to those theories historically?**

That third search is absolutely required by your new constitutional questions.

And I think these links already expose several **new first-order questions** we should burn into that constitution alongside your existing list:

> **When two traditions use language translated as “harmony,” “vibration,” “sound,” “word,” “ratio,” or “order,” are they actually asserting the same type of thing?**

> **Is the claimed correspondence analogical, mathematical, causal, ontological, theological, pedagogical, or aesthetic?**

> **Did an author say that \(A\) resembles \(B\), that \(A\) and \(B\) instantiate the same structure, or literally that \(A=B\)?**

> **When later science rejected an older theory, which component failed: its measurements, cosmology, causal mechanism, ontology, or only its interpretation?**

That last one could become extremely important. Mersenne is a good example: the speculative worldview and the developing science of acoustics coexist in the same program. The scientific component does not simply disappear when the broader cosmology loses authority. citeturn545029view0

Likewise BAO demonstrates why “old theory was wrong” cannot be translated into “there is no physically meaningful relationship between acoustical dynamics and cosmic structure.” There demonstrably is one in early-universe physics—but it is a very specific one, governed by plasma dynamics, not a license to import musical ratios into cosmology. citeturn545029view3

And Butler gives us perhaps the cleanest warning about language: historically, **“harmony” itself moves between metaphor, mathematical structure, organizing principle and asserted ontology**. citeturn545029view7

So, yes: **the missing links materially change the map.**

I would now move **Godwin, Kayser, Zorzi/Lorenzin, Mersenne, Ilnitchi, Butler, Bhartṛhari and Dyczkowski** into the serious prior-art/deep-study queue, with QFT and BAO maintained as scientific controls rather than support, and Alexander as a modern framing/prior-art branch.

The three unresolved links—`tgfaAAAAMAAJ`, the DDB item, and the Anuario `/view/149` record—should remain explicitly marked **UNRESOLVED**, not disappear from the corpus.
